answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but influence scarce: require every account to lock a stake that is slashed when a randomly audited task fails or peers prove collusion. A newcomer may wander freely, but cannot multiply voting power without locking more capital; splitting one stake across many names gains no weight. Audits must sample work independently to limit cartel capture. The basalt ledger records deposits and penalties, while ferrous escrow keeps the cost tangible: a sybil operator risks losing funds and paying repeated setup costs for each identity.
